transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’m not handling things right. Since my daughter left for basic training, it’s like something in me just fell apart. I come home from work and the house feels dead. I know that sounds dramatic, but it’s the word that keeps coming to me—dead. Too quiet, too empty. I’ll stand there with my keys in my hand and just not know what to do with myself.

And it’s spilling into everything. I’m crying in my truck before shifts, trying to pull myself together before I go in like nothing’s wrong. I’m a sheet metal worker, I weld, I’ve done the same kinds of jobs for years, and now I’m missing steps I shouldn’t be missing. Stuff I could practically do in my sleep before, I have to stop and think through, and even then I mess it up or lose track.

I’ve been snapping at the younger guys too, which I hate. They don’t deserve it. They ask a normal question or do something a little slow and I just bite their heads off, and then I feel awful after. That’s not how I want to be.

And outside of work… I used to go out on the water, and I used to work on my sculpture, and now I don’t. I just don’t see the point. I keep thinking I should pick it back up, or get out of the house, but then I just sit there. It’s like since she left, I can’t keep myself together.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?

It’s been about a month now. She left for basic training, and honestly it feels like it started right around then—like almost immediately after she was gone, I just wasn’t myself. At first I thought maybe it was just the first few days, you know, getting used to the quiet and the change, but it hasn’t really let up. So… yeah, about a month of feeling like this.
Are you still able to enjoy things that you used to find pleasurable before your daughter left?

No… not really. That’s actually one of the things that scares me, because I used to have things that were mine, you know? Like going out on the water—that used to clear my head. I could be out there for hours and come back feeling like I could breathe again. And my sculpture work, that was something I could just lose myself in. It made me feel steady.

But since my daughter left, I just… I don’t have it in me. I think about doing those things, and then it’s like my brain just says, “What’s the point?” I’ll look at the stuff for my sculpture and not even touch it. Or I’ll tell myself maybe I should get out of the house, go down by the water, do something besides just sitting there in all that quiet, and then I don’t. I just stay stuck.

The house feels so empty now—dead, almost—and I come home and it just hits me all over again. So no, I’m not really enjoying much of anything the way I used to.
Do you often feel guilty about things you've said or done, especially towards the younger guys you've been snapping at?

Yeah… I do. I feel terrible after. In the moment it’s like I’m already wound so tight I can’t take one more thing, and then one of the younger guys asks me something or does something a little off, and I just snap. I hear myself talking to them sharp, like I’m trying to cut them down, and I hate it even while it’s happening sometimes.

Then later I’ll be sitting in my truck or driving home and it just plays back in my head. They’re just trying to learn, you know? I used to be patient with them. I used to be the one who’d show them how to do a weld right or walk them through a job without making them feel stupid. And now, since my daughter left, it’s like I can’t keep myself together. I’m crying before shifts, I’m messing up steps on work I’ve done for years, and then I’m taking it out on people who don’t deserve it.

So yeah, guilty is… that’s exactly it. I feel ashamed of it. I don’t want to be that person at work.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Honestly… no, not really. I keep trying to think of something, because I don’t want to sound like I’ve just given up on everything, but since my daughter left for basic training it’s like the things that used to pull me out of myself just don’t work anymore.

I used to look forward to getting out on the water. That was my thing. Even if work was rough, I could tell myself, “Just get through the day and then you can go out there,” and that would help. And my sculpture work too—I could spend hours with it and feel like I was making something, like my hands knew what to do. But now I look at it and I just… I don’t see the point. I don’t go. I don’t pick it up. I just come home and the house feels so dead without her there, and I kind of shut down.

Even work, I’m barely holding it together. I’m crying in my truck before shifts, then I go in and miss steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I snap at the younger guys. So when I think about “looking forward” to something… I don’t know. Mostly I’m just trying to get through the day and get back home, even though being home feels awful too.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself since your daughter left for basic training?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that the right way. I don’t think I’ve had, like, a plan or anything I could point to and say, “This is what I’m going to do.” It’s more that everything feels so heavy sometimes that I get scared by how tired I am of feeling like this.

Since she left, there are moments where I’m just sitting there and it’s so quiet, and my mind kind of goes to dark places—not always specific, just… not wanting to be in that feeling anymore. But I don’t know if that’s the same as wanting to hurt myself. I haven’t really talked about it out loud, so I’m having trouble putting it into words.

I guess what I can say is it worries me that I’m even feeling this low. Like, I don’t recognize myself lately.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since your daughter left for basic training?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been paying close attention to the scale or anything like that. My clothes don’t feel so different that I’ve thought, “Oh, I’ve lost a bunch,” or “I’ve gained a lot,” but I also haven’t exactly been checking.

I mean, since she left, I’ve been kind of just getting through the day, so things like weighing myself or noticing numbers… they’re not really on my mind. If there has been a change, I don’t know that I could tell you how much. Nothing obvious that I’ve noticed, I guess.
Have you been having thoughts about death frequently since your daughter left?

I’m not sure how to separate that from what I was trying to say before. Like… I don’t sit there every hour thinking about death in a clear way, if that’s what you mean. It’s not like I’m making some kind of plan or picturing something specific all the time.

But since she left, my mind does go to these really dark places sometimes. It’s more like… everything feels so empty and final for a moment, and I’ll think about how tired I am of feeling this way, or how I don’t know how I’m supposed to keep feeling like this day after day. And then I scare myself, because I don’t usually think like that. I’ve always been someone who just keeps moving, keeps working, handles things.

So “frequently”… I don’t know. Maybe more than I want to admit. Not constant, but enough that it bothers me. Enough that I’m sitting here telling you about it because I don’t feel right pretending it hasn’t been happening.
Are there any small things that still bring you some joy or pleasure?

There used to be, yeah. I mean, that’s part of what scares me, because I’m not someone who just sits around doing nothing. I used to love getting out on the water whenever I could, even if it was just for a little while. That was always the thing that would clear my head, you know? The noise, the work, the smell of it… it made me feel like myself.

And I had this sculpture I was working on, metal pieces, kind of rough-looking but it meant something to me. I’d come home from work and mess with it, even if I was tired. But since my daughter left for basic training, I just… I look at that stuff and I don’t see the point. I haven’t been going out on the water. I haven’t really touched the sculpture. It’s like all the color got drained out of things.

I come home and the house feels dead. That’s the only way I can explain it. Just too quiet, like the whole place is holding its breath, and I can’t keep myself together. Even work isn’t giving me that normal rhythm anymore. I’ve been crying in my truck before shifts, trying to get it out before I walk in, and then I still mess up—missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I snap at the younger guys over stupid things, and then I feel bad because they didn’t do anything wrong.

So… small things that bring me joy? Not really. Or if they do, I can’t seem to feel it the way I used to.
Are there any activities or things that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really… I mean, I know I kind of said that already, but that’s the part I keep circling back to. Things I used to enjoy just don’t land the same anymore.

I used to like going out on the water. That was my way of getting my head straight. And I had this sculpture I was working on—metal, kind of pieced together, nothing fancy, but it mattered to me. I’d come home and work on it even after being on my feet all day. Now I come home and it’s like the house is just… dead. Too quiet. I look at the sculpture and I don’t even pick up the tools. I think about going out on the water and I just can’t make myself do it. I don’t see the point.

Since my daughter left for basic training, everything feels off. I can’t keep myself together the way I normally do. I’ll sit in my truck before a shift crying, trying to get it out before anyone sees me, and then I go in and I’m still not right. I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, stuff that should be automatic. And then I snap at the younger guys over little things, and I hate that, because it’s not really them.

So, no… I don’t think there’s much I’m enjoying right now. It feels like I’m just getting through things, not actually taking pleasure in anything.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt better since your daughter left for basic training?

Not really, no. I mean… maybe there are tiny moments where I’m distracted for a little while, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a real stretch where I felt better.

It’s been about a month since she left for basic training, and honestly I feel like I’ve been struggling like this pretty much since then. It’s not like I had a bad day and then bounced back. It settled in after she left, and I keep waiting for it to ease up or for me to get used to the house being different, but it hasn’t really happened.

So… no, I can’t point to a period of time where I felt like myself again. It’s been about a month of this.
Are there any activities that you've tried to do since your daughter left that you thought might bring you some pleasure, but didn't?

Yeah… I have tried, a few times. Mostly the things I used to count on, I guess. Like going out on the water — I kept thinking, “If I can just get myself out there, maybe it’ll knock something loose, maybe I’ll feel normal for an hour.” But I haven’t really been able to follow through. I’ll get as far as thinking about it, maybe looking at the gear or the weather, and then it just feels like too much effort for something that won’t matter anyway.

And the sculpture… that’s the one that bothers me because that was mine, you know? I’d work with metal all day and still come home and want to mess with this thing, like it gave the day some kind of shape. Since my daughter left, I’ve stood there and looked at it, picked up a tool maybe, and then I just put it back down. I don’t see the point. It just sits there, half-finished, and it makes the house feel even more dead somehow.

It’s like I come home and everything is too quiet, and I can’t get myself together. Then I’m crying in my truck before work, trying to get it out before my shift, and I still go in and mess up steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. Then I snap at the younger guys over nothing, and I feel awful about it. So even the things I thought might help… they just don’t. They feel empty now.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I do. I know I’ve kind of been saying that, but yes, that’s exactly what it feels like. It’s not just that I’m tired or busy or something. It’s like the interest is gone, or the part of me that cared about those things isn’t there right now.

Since my daughter left for basic training, I come home and the house just feels dead. Too quiet. I used to go out on the water, and that was something I really enjoyed — it cleared my head. And I had my sculpture, this metal piece I was working on, and I used to actually look forward to it. Now I’ll look at it sitting there and I just don’t pick up the tools. I think about going out on the water and I don’t even get myself moving. I just… don’t see the point.

And it’s not like I’m holding it together great otherwise. I’m crying in my truck before shifts, trying to get myself together before I go in. Then at work I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I’ve been snapping at the younger guys over little things. That’s not how I usually am.

So, yes. I’ve lost interest in the things I used to enjoy. It all feels empty right now.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since your daughter left for basic training?

I don’t really know. I haven’t weighed myself or anything, so I can’t say I’ve lost a significant amount.

My clothes don’t feel dramatically different, at least not that I’ve noticed. I mean, I’m not exactly paying close attention to that right now. I might be eating a little differently here and there, but in terms of actual weight loss… I don’t have a number for you, and I haven’t had someone say, “You look like you’ve lost weight,” or anything like that.

So… no, not that I can tell.
Do you feel sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day, since your daughter left for basic training?

Yeah… most of the day, pretty much every day. I don’t know if “sad” is even the whole word for it. It’s sad, yes, but it’s also this empty feeling, like something got pulled out of the house and out of me at the same time.

Since my daughter left for basic training, I come home and it just feels… dead. Too quiet. I’ll walk in and there’s nobody there, and I know she’s doing what she’s supposed to do, I know that, but knowing it doesn’t make the house feel any less hollow. I keep thinking I should be able to handle it better, but I can’t seem to keep myself together.

It follows me into the day too. I’m crying in my truck before shifts, trying to get it out before I go inside. And then I’m not right at work — I’m missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I’ll snap at the younger guys over nothing, and afterward I feel terrible because that’s not how I want to be.

And when I get home, I don’t even do the things that used to help. I don’t go out on the water. I don’t work on my sculpture. I’ll look at it and just think, what’s the point? So… yes. It’s there most of the day. It’s not just a moment here and there.
Have you noticed any change in how your clothes fit since your daughter left for basic training?

I honestly haven’t really noticed. I mean, I put my work clothes on and they still go on, my jeans still button, my shirts don’t feel like they’re hanging off me or anything obvious like that.

I guess I haven’t been checking myself in the mirror much or paying attention to whether things are looser or tighter. I’ve just been getting dressed and getting through the day. So if there’s been some small change, I couldn’t really tell you. Nothing has stood out to me with how my clothes fit.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight since your daughter left for basic training?

I don’t know. I really don’t. I haven’t weighed myself, so I can’t say whether it’s more than 5% or not.

I mean, I know that’s a specific number, and if I had been tracking it I could answer you better, but I just haven’t. I get dressed, my clothes seem to fit about the same as far as I can tell, and nobody’s said anything to me like I look thinner. So… I can’t honestly say I’ve lost that much weight. I don’t have anything that tells me that.
Have you noticed any significant change in your appetite since your daughter left for basic training?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been paying close attention to it in a way where I could say, “Yes, I’m eating a lot less,” or “No, it’s exactly the same.”

I mean, I still eat. I go through the motions with meals when I need to, and if something’s in front of me I’ll usually pick at it or eat it. But I couldn’t tell you if my appetite has changed in some big, clear way. I haven’t been tracking it, and it hasn’t jumped out at me like, “Oh, I’m never hungry anymore,” or “I’m eating constantly.”

It’s more like… everything feels kind of off, so it’s hard to separate what’s appetite and what’s just me not paying attention to normal routines. So I guess the honest answer is I haven’t noticed a significant change, not one I can clearly point to.
Have your feelings of sadness and emptiness lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks since your daughter left for basic training?

Yeah… I mean, most days, yes. I don’t know if I could clock it exactly like “every minute of every day for two weeks,” but since she left it’s been there a lot. It’s like I come home and the house feels dead. Not just quiet, but dead, like the air’s gone out of it.

I can hold it together in front of people sometimes, but then I’ll be sitting in my truck before a shift and just start crying, and I hate that. I’m not somebody who usually does that. I’m supposed to go in and do my job, keep my head on straight, and instead I’m wiping my face and trying to look normal before I walk in.

And it follows me around. I’ll be at work and miss steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, stuff I shouldn’t even have to think about. Then I get mad and snap at the younger guys, and afterward I feel awful because they didn’t do anything to deserve it.

So… yeah, it’s not just a little sad moment here and there. It’s most of the day, most days. I’ve stopped going out on the water, I haven’t touched my sculpture, and those were the things that usually made me feel like myself. Lately I just don’t see the point.
Have your feelings of sadness and emptiness lasted for at least two weeks since your daughter left for basic training?

Yes. It’s been at least two weeks. Honestly, it’s been closer to a month now since my daughter left for basic training, and I’ve been struggling like this pretty much since then.

It wasn’t like I had one bad weekend and then got back to normal. From when she left, it just sort of settled in, and it hasn’t really let up the way I thought it would. I kept thinking maybe after a few days I’d adjust, or once I got used to the routine it wouldn’t feel so heavy, but… it’s been weeks now. About a month. So yes, definitely more than two weeks.
